title: Third Wave Coffee Raises Rs 408 Crore as WestBridge Capital Doubles Down on India’s Cafe Boom
excerpt: Bengaluru-based coffee chain secures fresh funding from existing backers at a valuation of up to $500 million, nearly tripling its 2023 valuation as India’s specialty coffee market heats up.
body:
• Third Wave Coffee has raised Rs 408 crore (approximately $48 million) in a funding round led by existing backer WestBridge Capital, with participation from Creaegis.
  • The round is part of a larger $80–100 million fundraise at a valuation of $400–500 million, up sharply from the $155 million valuation in its 2023 Series C round.
  • The Bengaluru-based chain reported revenue of Rs 268.6 crore in FY25 and narrowed losses to Rs 94.4 crore from Rs 152.4 crore a year earlier.
  • India’s organized coffee market is projected to grow at a 15–20% CAGR to reach $2.6–3.2 billion within two years, drawing aggressive investment from domestic and global players.

WestBridge and Creaegis Double Down

Third Wave Coffee, the Bengaluru-based specialty cafe chain, has raised Rs 408 crore in a funding round led by WestBridge Capital, with participation from Creaegis, according to multiple reports. The round forms part of a larger $80–100 million fundraise that includes both primary capital and secondary share sales, Mint reported, citing three people familiar with the matter.

The transaction is largely an internal round with existing backers increasing their stakes, with WestBridge writing the larger cheque. The funding is expected to close at a valuation of $400–500 million, a sharp jump from the approximately $155 million valuation at which the company raised its $35 million Series C round in late 2023, according to Tracxn data cited by Mint.

Expansion Plans and Improving Unit Economics

The primary capital will fund Third Wave Coffee’s expansion across India. The company, founded in 2017 by Sushant Goel, Ayush Bathwal, and Anirudh Sharma, operates cafes in Bengaluru, Delhi, Mumbai, Pune, Hyderabad, and other cities. Under new CEO Rajat Luthra — who previously oversaw KFC India operations for more than a decade — the company plans to add at least 50 new stores and expand to cities including Chennai.

Heisetasse Beverages Pvt. Ltd., which operates the brand, reported revenue from operations of Rs 268.6 crore in FY25, up from Rs 241.3 crore the prior year. More importantly, losses narrowed significantly to Rs 94.4 crore from Rs 152.4 crore in FY24, according to filings sourced by Tofler from the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. The company is also scaling up its central roastery capacity threefold to supply its growing store network and expand into offline retail channels.

“We will continue to be a coffee-first brand. We should add at least 50 stores by the end of the financial year — that’s the minimum we are looking at.”

— Rajat Luthra, CEO, Third Wave Coffee

India’s Specialty Coffee Arms Race

The fundraise comes amid a surge of investor interest in India’s organized cafe and specialty beverage market. Blue Tokai Coffee Roasters raised Rs 175 crore in an extension of its Series D round led by Anicut Capital earlier in August. AbCoffee, the Mumbai-based grab-and-go chain, raised Rs 61 crore in a pre-Series B round led by Kliff Ventures. Chaayos was reportedly planning a $50–70 million raise in April.

India’s coffee market, valued at approximately $1.2 billion in 2023, is projected to expand at a compounded annual growth rate of 15–20% to reach $2.6–3.2 billion within two years, according to a report by Redseer. The broader food services market is valued at $80 billion and growing at 10–11% annually.

Third Wave Coffee competes with domestic players like Blue Tokai and Subko as well as international chains including Starbucks, Tim Hortons, and Pret A Manger, which have expanded aggressively in India over the past few years.

What’s Next

The fundraise positions Third Wave Coffee for accelerated growth at a time when India’s cafe culture is shifting rapidly. The premium coffee segment — priced above Rs 200 per cup — is growing at 15–20% annually, while the mid-range segment (Rs 100–200) is expanding even faster at 35–40%, according to Forbes India. With WestBridge’s continued backing and improved unit economics, the company appears positioned for an eventual public listing, though no timeline has been disclosed.
